sections.overview: This steppe antelope is native to Central Asia, with populations in several countries.
sections.identification: Its most distinctive feature is a swollen, flexible nose that projects beyond the mouth.
sections.habitat: It inhabits dry steppe and semi-desert.
sections.diet: It eats grasses and herbs, with food varying by season.
sections.behavior: It forms herds and moves seasonally to find grazing and avoid deep snow.
sections.reproduction: Females give birth to one or two calves, often together in open areas.
sections.ecology: The unusual nose helps condition inhaled air in the species’ sharply seasonal steppe climate.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment was downlisted to Near Threatened in 2023.
